questions.q: What did the story of the badly designed ads demonstrate?
a: Inspired employees matter more than inspiring leaders
Leaders should personally fix every visible problem
Weekend work should be expected from all engineers
Advertising quality matters more than search results
questions.why: Lesson 1 says Page simply pointed out the problem, and engineers who were already inspired fixed it over the weekend.

questions.q: How does Google attract the kind of people it calls smart creatives?
a: By building a culture with inspiring values and purpose
By offering the highest salaries in the industry
By hiring only graduates of elite universities
By promising rapid promotions and job titles
questions.why: Lesson 1 says inspiring values attract ambitious, smart people who are not driven mainly by money.

questions.q: What is Google's attitude toward slow decisions?
a: They are fine as long as everyone supports the outcome
They should be avoided because speed always wins
They should be settled by the most senior person
They should be postponed until the market decides
questions.why: Lesson 2 says decisions may take time, but everyone must be convinced so they commit fully once a choice is made.

questions.q: What happened when Sergey Brin disagreed with an engineer's proposal?
a: The whole team eventually backed the engineer's more convincing plan
Brin overruled the engineer and ordered his own plan
The project was canceled until a consensus could form
The engineer was moved to a different team
questions.why: Lesson 2 says Brin let half the team try each side, and everyone ultimately chose the engineer's approach.

Twenty percent of profits shared with employees
A fifth of the year reserved for company retreats
A rule that meetings take up part of each day
